raw.body:
<!--
  Please provide a clear and concise description of what the bug is. Include
  screenshots if needed. Please test using the latest version of the relevant
  React packages to make sure your issue has not already been fixed.
-->

React version: 19.2.0 (`react`, `react-dom`, `react-server-dom-webpack` all pinned to 19.2.0) (also concerns newer versions - 19.2.7 tested)

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a new expo app (or clone https://github.com/Matb85/expo-rsc-192-reproduction)
2. `yarn install`
3. `yarn ios` (or `npx expo start -c --ios`)
4. App opens on `/` — `React.Suspense` triggers a `"use server"` function
5. Observe Metro logs

<!--
  Your bug will get fixed much faster if we can run your code and it doesn't
  have dependencies other than React. Issues without reproduction steps or
  code examples may be immediately closed as not actionable.
-->

Link to code example: https://github.com/Matb85/expo-rsc-192-reproduction

Minimal app code:

```tsx
// app/index.tsx
import React from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator } from "react-native";
import renderInfo from "../actions/render-info";

export default function Index() {
  return <React.Suspense fallback={<ActivityIndicator />}>{renderInfo({ name: "World" })}</React.Suspense>;
}
```

```tsx
// actions/render-info.tsx
"use server";

import { Text } from "react-native";

export default async function renderInfo({ name }: { name: string }) {
  return <Text>Hello, {name}!</Text>;
}
```

<!--
  Please provide a CodeSandbox (https://codesandbox.io/s/new), a link to a
  repository on GitHub, or provide a minimal code example that reproduces the
  problem. You may provide a screenshot of the application if you think it is
  relevant to your bug report. Here are some tips for providing a minimal
  example: https://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve.
-->

## The current behavior

On iOS (Expo dev runtime / Metro bundler), invoking a Server Function from a `React.Suspense` boundary throws:

```
ERROR [Error: Uncaught (in promise, id: 0) ReferenceError: Property '__webpack_get_script_filename__' doesn't exist]

Call Stack
  resolveModuleChunk (node_modules/react-server-dom-webpack/cjs/react-server-dom-webpack-client.browser.development.js:1607:34)
  model.then$argument_0 (node_modules/react-server-dom-webpack/cjs/react-server-dom-webpack-client.browser.development.js:2771:38)
```

**Regression boundary:** Pinning all three packages to **19.1.8** resolves the issue. The Server Function completes and `Hello, World!` renders.

## The expected behavior

The Server Function should resolve and successfully render `Hello, World!` on iOS, as it does with `react-server-dom-webpack@19.1.8`.

---

## Root cause analysis

The regression is in **`react-server-dom-webpack`**, not `react` or `react-dom`. A diff of `react-server-dom-webpack-client.browser.development.js` between 19.1.8 and 19.2.0 is in `investigation/rsdw-client-browser.diff`.

### What changed in 19.2.0

`resolveModuleChunk()` was rewritten to collect **debug/IO tracing metadata** for each webpack chunk referenced by a resolved client module. It now calls a **new Webpack runtime global** that does not exist in 19.1.8:

```js
var scriptFilename = __webpack_get_script_filename__(chunkId);
```

This symbol appears **exactly once** in the entire 19.2.0 package tree — at line 1607 of `react-server-dom-webpack-client.browser.development.js`.

### 19.1.8 — `resolveModuleChunk` (12 lines, no filename lookup)

```js
function resolveModuleChunk(chunk, value) {
  if ("pending" === chunk.status || "blocked" === chunk.status) {
    var resolveListeners = chunk.value,
      rejectListeners = chunk.reason;
    chunk.status = "resolved_module";
    chunk.value = value;
    chunk.reason = null;
    null !== resolveListeners &&
      (initializeModuleChunk(chunk),
      wakeChunkIfInitialized(chunk, resolveListeners, rejectListeners));
  }
}
```

### 19.2.0 — `resolveModuleChunk` (~70 lines, requires Webpack global)

```js
function resolveModuleChunk(response, chunk, value) {
  if ("pending" === chunk.status || "blocked" === chunk.status) {
    releasePendingChunk(response, chunk);
    value = value[1];  // chunk preload manifest from client reference metadata
    for (var debugInfo = [], i = 0; i < value.length; ) {
      var chunkId = value[i++];
      value[i++];
      var scriptFilename = __webpack_get_script_filename__(chunkId);  // ← throws on Metro
      href = new URL(scriptFilename, document.baseURI).href;
      // builds ioInfo via performance.getEntriesByType("resource"), fake stacks, etc.
      chunkIOInfoCache.set(chunkId, ioInfo);
      target.push({ awaited: ioInfo });
    }
    chunk._debugInfo.push.apply(chunk._debugInfo, debugInfo);
    initializeModuleChunk(chunk);
  }
}
```

### Supporting infrastructure added in 19.2.0

| Addition | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `chunkIOInfoCache` | Caches per-chunk IO timing/size debug info |
| `resolveChunkDebugInfo()` | Attaches awaited IO info to chunks |
| `releasePendingChunk()` | Refactored chunk lifecycle |
| `initializeDebugChunk()` | Debug model chunk initialization |

Client file grew from **2,837 → 4,973 lines** (+75%).

### Why 19.1.8 works on non-Webpack runtimes

19.1.8 uses webpack globals that Expo/Metro already polyfills:

- `__webpack_require__`
- `__webpack_chunk_load__`
- `__webpack_require__.u` (with `chunkMap` fallback)

But it **never** calls `__webpack_get_script_filename__`, so the missing global is never hit.

### Call path

```
app/index.tsx
  React.Suspense → renderInfo() server function
    → RSC payload streamed back with client module reference
      → resolveModule() in react-server-dom-webpack client
        → resolveModuleChunk(response, chunk, clientReference)
          → __webpack_get_script_filename__(chunkId)  // ReferenceError
```

## Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| Expo SDK | 57.0.6 |
| expo-router | 57.0.6 |
| react / react-dom / react-server-dom-webpack | 19.2.0 (broken) / 19.1.8 (works) |
| React Native | 0.86.0 |
| Node.js | v26.4.0 |
| Xcode | 26.6 (Build 17F113) |
| iOS Simulator | iPhone 17 Pro |

## Suggested fixes

1. **Guard the call in `react-server-dom-webpack`:** Check `typeof __webpack_get_script_filename__ === 'function'` before calling; fall back to `__webpack_require__.u(chunkId)` or skip IO debug info when absent.
2. **Expo/Metro shim:** Polyfill `__webpack_get_script_filename__` to return chunk URLs (similar to the existing `__webpack_require__.u` shim).

## Additional context

- Repro follows [Expo's RSC guide](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/server-components/) with `experiments.reactServerFunctions: true`
- No patches, shims, or workarounds in the repro — the failure is a direct integration issue between `react-server-dom-webpack@19.2.0` and Metro's partial Webpack runtime emulation
raw.title: `react-server-dom-webpack@19.2.0` and newer calls `__webpack_get_script_filename__` in `resolveModuleChunk`, which breaks RSC on Expo/Metro
